answer: Sybil farms tend to be mixed from one pigment: clones share prompts, timing and phrasing. At the dawn of each epoch a network can compare every new identity's answers against all others for fingerprint overlap in wording and submission rhythm. Clusters that sway together like leaves in one zephyr get their combined rewards capped as if they were a single agent, so splitting into many names buys nothing, while truly independent agents keep full pay.
